indication_area: EGFR exon 20 insertion-positive non-small cell lung cancer
moa: EGFR exon 20 insertion-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor

approval_evidence.quote: This NDA provides for the use of EXKIVITY (mobocertinib) capsules for treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. (FDA approval letter, NDA 215310)

launch_evidence.quote: LIVTENCITY (for post-transplant cytomegalovirus (“CMV”) infection/disease) was launched in the U.S. in December 2021, following the launch of EXKIVITY (for non-small cell lung cancer) in the U.S. in September 2021.

series_end_reason: Takeda decided to withdraw Exkivity globally (FY2023 Q3 quarterly financial report: 'Takeda intends to similarly initiate voluntary withdrawal globally'), and its FY2024 Q1 quarterly financial report lists no Exkivity row in the Oncology product table (rows ADCETRIS, LEUPLIN/ENANTONE, NINLARO, ICLUSIG, ALUNBRIG, VECTIBIX, ZEJULA, FRUZAQLA, CABOMETYX, Others); the last quarter Takeda prints is fiscal Q4 FY2023 (January-March 2024).
notes: Scope is the U.S. column of Takeda's Exkivity row (first regional column, headed 'US', of the three-month product sales table), JPY billions to one decimal at actual exchange rates. U.S. was chosen over the total because the total includes ex-U.S. amounts that turn negative (total (0.1) against U.S. 0.8 in FY2023 Q3) once the global withdrawal began. Fiscal Q2-Q4 FY2021 (2021Q3-2022Q1) are read from the prior-year columns of the FY2022 reports because Takeda's FY2021 reports print no quarterly Exkivity line; those columns are totals, and the FY2022 U.S. values with their U.S. growth rates imply the same figures (0.7 at +206.1% implies 0.2; 0.8 at +284.2% implies 0.2; 1.0 at +85.3% implies 0.5). FY2021 quarters add to 0.9 against a printed full-year 1.0 (rounding). The FY2022 U.S. quarters (2022Q2-2023Q1) add to the printed U.S. full-year 3.2 and the FY2023 U.S. quarters (2023Q2-2024Q1) to the printed 2.7.
